# Refunds

You can request a refund for any annual plan within 30 days of the charge. Monthly plans are not refundable, but you can cancel at any time and keep access until the end of the billing period.

To request a refund, open Settings, choose Billing, and select the charge you want refunded. Re

funds go back to the original payment method and usually arrive within 5 to 10 business days, depending on your bank.

If you paid by bank transfer, we need your account details before we can send the money back. Reply to the refund confirmation email with the account holder name and IBAN.

Refunds
are not available for add-on usage that has already been consumed, such as extra SMS reminders or additional storage.

# Billing cycles and plan changes

Orchard bills in advance. Monthly plans renew on the same day each month, and annual plans renew on the anniversary of the day you subscribed. The renewal date is shown at the top of the Billing page.

When you upgrade in the middle of a cycle, the new plan starts

immediately and we charge the price difference for the days that remain. When you downgrade, the lower price applies from the next renewal date.

If a renewal payment fails, we retry the card three times over seven days. After the third failed attempt the workspace becomes read-only until a payment

succeeds.

You can switch between monthly and annual billing at any time. Switching to annual billing applies a discount equal to two months of the monthly price.

# Single sign-on (SSO)

Single sign-on lets your team log in to Orchard through your identity provider instead of a password. SSO is available on the Business plan and uses the SAML 2.0 standard.

To set up SSO, a workspace owner opens Settings, chooses Security, and selects Configure SAML. Copy the

ACS URL and the entity ID shown there into your identity provider, then paste the provider's metadata URL back into Orchard.

Before you enforce SSO, test the connection with one user. Once SSO is enforced, password login is disabled for everyone except workspace owners, who keep a password as a re

covery path.

New users who sign in through SSO for the first time are created automatically with the Member role. This is called just-in-time provisioning and can be turned off on the same Security page.

# API keys

API keys let scripts and integrations call the Orchard API on behalf of your workspace. Each key belongs to the user who created it and has the same permissions as that user.

To create a key, open Settings, choose Developers, and select New API key. The full key is shown only once, so c

opy it to a secret manager before you close the dialog.

Rotate a key by creating a new one, updating your integration, and then revoking the old key. Revoking takes effect within one minute and cannot be undone.

Send the key in the Authorization header as a bearer token. Never put a key in a URL o
r commit it to source control, because keys found in public repositories are revoked automatically.

# API rate limits

The Orchard API allows 120 requests per minute for each API key. Bulk endpoints, such as invoice import, count every item in the batch as one request.

When you exceed the limit, the API responds with HTTP status 429 and a Retry-After header that gives the number of seconds to wai

t. Requests that receive a 429 response are not processed.

The best way to stay under the limit is to back off and retry with increasing delays, and to use the bulk endpoints instead of many single calls. The response headers show how many requests remain in the current window.

Higher limits are a
vailable on the Business plan. Contact support with the key name and the request volume you expect.

# Exporting your data

You can export invoices, customers and payments as CSV files at any time. Open Settings, choose Data, and select Export. Large exports are prepared in the background and emailed to you as a download link.

Download links expire after 24 hours. If a link has expired, start the

export again from the Data page.

A full workspace export also includes attachments and PDF copies of every invoice, packed into a single ZIP archive. Only workspace owners can start a full export.

Exports use UTC for all timestamps and a period as the decimal separator, regardless of the display s
ettings in your workspace.

# Resetting your password

If you have forgotten your password, select Forgot password on the login page and enter your email address. We send a reset link that is valid for one hour.

If the email does not arrive, check your spam folder and confirm that you used the address on your Orchard account.

Reset emails are not sent to addresses that have no account.

For security, resetting a password signs you out on every device. You will need to log in again with the new password, and with your second factor if two-factor authentication is on.

Accounts in a workspace that enforces single sign-on
do not have a password. Ask your workspace owner if you cannot log in through your identity provider.

# User roles and permissions

Every person in a workspace has exactly one role. The role decides what they can see and change:

- Owner: full access, including billing and deleting the workspace
- Admin: manages users, settings and all invoices
- Member: creates and edits their own invoices

Only an

owner can change another person's role. A workspace must always have at least one owner, so the last owner cannot be removed or downgraded.

Members cannot see invoices created by other members unless an admin shares a customer with them. Shared customers appear in the member's customer list with a

small link icon.

To invite someone, open Settings, choose Team, and enter their email address. Invitations expire after seven days and can be sent again from the same page.

# Webhooks

Webhooks notify your server when something happens in Orchard, such as an invoice being paid or a customer being created. Each webhook is an HTTPS endpoint that receives a JSON payload.

Every delivery is signed. Compute an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body with your webhook secret and

compare it with the value in the Orchard-Signature header before you trust the payload.

If your endpoint does not return a 2xx status within ten seconds, we retry the delivery up to eight times with increasing delays over about 24 hours. After that the event is marked as failed.

You can replay fa
iled events from the Developers page for 30 days. Events are delivered at least once, so make your handler idempotent by storing the event ID.

# Deleting a workspace

Deleting a workspace permanently removes its invoices, customers, attachments and users. Only an owner can delete a workspace, and the action requires typing the workspace name to confirm.

After you confirm, the workspace enters a 14-day grace period. During this time nobody

can log in, but an owner can cancel the deletion by contacting support.

When the grace period ends, the data is erased from our production systems. Encrypted backups are kept for a further 35 days and are then overwritten.

Tax law in some countries requires you to keep invoices for several years.
Export your data before you delete the workspace, because we cannot recover it afterwards.

# Two-factor authentication

Two-factor authentication adds a second step when you log in: a six-digit code from an authenticator app. Turn it on under Settings, Security, Two-factor authentication.

When you enable it, Orchard shows ten recovery codes. Each recovery code works once. Store them some

where safe, because they are the only way back in if you lose your phone.

If you have lost both your phone and your recovery codes, a workspace owner can reset your second factor from the Team page. Owners who are locked out must contact support and verify their identity.

Admins can require two-fa
ctor authentication for every member of a workspace. Members who have not set it up are asked to do so the next time they log in.

# Creating and sending invoices

To create an invoice, select New invoice, pick a customer, and add at least one line item. Invoice numbers are assigned in sequence when the invoice is sent, not when the draft is created.

You can send an invoice by email directly from Orchard or download it as a PD

F. Emailed invoices include a payment link if online payments are enabled.

A sent invoice cannot be edited. To correct a mistake, issue a credit note for the original invoice and create a new one. This keeps your numbering complete for audits.

Automatic reminders can be sent before and after the d
ue date. Set the schedule under Settings, Invoicing, Reminders.
